segments: Chronography of Bar Hebraeus.
And they said:
"It is not right for us now to engage the Franks in the strength of their gathering,
but let us weaken their country (their territories) a little.
And when they are dispersed,
then it will be easy for us to overthrow each one of them individually."
Saladin did not accept [this] from them, but said:
"When again will such a great gathering be assembled for me? Rather, take courage, play the man, and attack;
and whatever the Lord wills, He does."
And immediately he mounted and had his forces mount,
and they went and encamped on the Jordan around the Sea of Tiberias.
And the Franks gathered at a place named Sepphoris.
And both sides remained for days facing each other without stirring up battle.
Then Saladin sent a detachment from his forces by a secret route at night against the city of Tiberias.
And when morning dawned,
they assaulted and entered the city,
and they put sword and fire to it.
And the queen took refuge in the fortress.
Now when Guy, her husband, heard [this],
his joints were loosed,
and again he encouraged himself and the Franks,
and they all rode out with fierce impetuosity against the Arabs.
And when it was evening,
both camps encamped close to each other,
and all that night not a single man among them slept.
And because the Arabs held the bank of the Jordan,
the thirst of the Franks became severe during that night,
and they had no place to drink;
then they were all the more sharpened for battle.
And when morning dawned,
and the Arabs saw the courage of the Franks,
that they cast themselves [forward] like wasps,
and did not turn back,
they were greatly afraid and lost heart,
and their knees trembled.
Now when Saladin saw their slackness,
he ran into the midst,
and shouted with a loud voice,
and let them hear words mixed with honey and bitterness,
that is to say, encouragements and threats.
Then one of Saladin's own servants, a young warrior whose name was Manguras,
took courage and came out from the battle lines of the Arabs.
And when he was between both sides,
another warrior from the Franks advanced to meet him,
and struck him with a spear and threw him from his horse.
And he leaned down, seized him by his braid,
and dragged him toward the line...
the Queen of Jerusalem,
but the wife of Raymond, Count of Tripoli. 2
